method: Independent recomputation in Python (stdlib) from the 24 committed records.jsonl.gz by validator/recompute.py, written from PROTOCOL.md, the record format and the documented formulas of band.rs (priced_gae(w) = G - C + w (U + n_C), C from docs/ic/calibration.json, U including counted table_insert_attempts) and compare.rs/stats.rs (ratio of totals over (workload, round) pairs; linearised t on (session, workload) clusters, log-scale interval; two-stage cluster bootstrap with the validator's own RNG), without reading analysis/*.mjs, analysis/correctness.py logic beyond its committed diff, summary.json or results.json until own-numbers.json was written. Correctness by a generic deep diff of every -p record against its twin (every round incl. warm-up). Scalar certificates by own prime-field and GF(2^n) arithmetic. Build adds against the closed form and an independent combinatorial model of the recursion (prune_model.py). Replays: ecbench verify --replay-all on all 24 sessions, on 24 pre-prune sibling sessions (default-off path), and on three fresh sessions with nonce-derived seeds (B15, P24, and nonce-chosen P22).

code_audit_6d6aa93b8f.loop_bound: extend() at depth d iterates abscissae ai < end, end = len - (k - d - 1) with prune (len otherwise); a partial ending at ai can be completed only if len - 1 - ai >= k - d - 1, i.e. ai < len - (k - d - 1): the bound skips exactly the partials that cannot reach k summands; at the last depth (d = k - 1) end = len, so no insert is skipped
code_audit_6d6aa93b8f.uncounted_ops: every add is g.add(&mut self.build_ops, ..) and the oracle merges build_ops into oracle_setup (plugins.rs); pruning only removes calls, adds no group operation outside the counter
code_audit_6d6aa93b8f.default_off: prune = false gives end = groups.len(), .take(len) is the identity: the iteration is unchanged; params.flag('prune') is false when the key is absent

scale: the saved adds are lower-level partials of the k-sum build; their share of the build is 36% at a = 7 (k = 5) and falls roughly as 1/a^2 (10% at a = 12, 3% at a = 20, 0.1% at a = 100); the gain is a constant-factor saving that vanishes at larger bases and does not change any exponent

the ksum5 headline compares against unpruned ksum5, which at w = 0 is not the cheapest unpruned k-sum arm on 7 of 8 rows (P20, P22, P24, B15, B18, B21, B24: ksum4 is); cheapest-to-cheapest arm the gain is 0.939-0.973 at w = 0 and 0.953-0.987 at w = 1, and the cheapest k-sum arm's gap to rho-neg at w = 0 goes from 5.22-6.00 to 4.97-5.65 (checks.best_arm_framing)
